name: Clay
verdict: No OAuth exists: use your own API key from a service user, since the developer platform is on all plans and API use consumes Clay credits. Customers would paste their own key; same day.
needGuide: No — just create an API key under API and CLI; note the Tables API is Enterprise only.

auth.detail: Public API (https://api.clay.com/public/v0) with a personal API key in the clay-api-key header, tied to a Clay user and that user's workspace access. Keys are shown only once. A clay CLI and an agent plugin exist. No OAuth documented. Outbound webhooks: signed HMAC-SHA256 POST (X-Clay-Signature) when a routine run finishes.

effort.timeToProduction: Same day; Enterprise features need sales

approval.gate: None for OAuth because none exists. The developer platform is on all plans including free and trial, and API use consumes the same credits as in-product actions. Table reads with filters, joins or paging beyond 100 rows need the Enterprise API table sync.

scopes.why: No scopes documented; access equals the key owner's workspace permissions.
scopes.summary: No scopes documented. Access equals the key owner's workspace permissions.

cost: Included on all plans; consumes Clay credits and actions; Tables API is Enterprise only
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any Clay user with workspace access can create a key, which acts with that user's permissions (specific roles not documented). Use a dedicated service-user account rather than a personal one so keys survive staff changes (likely sensible; not documented).
Where you register: Clay app, then API and CLI, then API keys (or run clay api-keys create --name <name>)
Cost: Included on all plans; consumes Clay credits and actions; Tables API is Enterprise only

registerAt.path: Clay app, then API and CLI, then API keys (or run clay api-keys create --name <name>)

steps.do: Create or choose a company Clay workspace and a dedicated service user
Create an API key in the app under API and CLI, then API keys, and store it as a secret
Call GET /public/v0/me with the clay-api-key header to validate the key and workspace
Run a routine or search and register an outbound webhook with clay webhooks create <url>; save the signing secret
Verify X-Clay-Signature with constant-time HMAC-SHA256 and fall back to polling run results
For Tables, contact Clay about the Enterprise plan

roles.team: Any Clay user with workspace access can create a key, which acts with that user's permissions (specific roles not documented). Use a dedicated service-user account rather than a personal one so keys survive staff changes (likely sensible; not documented).
roles.customer: None. Customers cannot connect via OAuth; they would paste their own API key, which acts as their user.

testing: Use a free or trial workspace; call GET /me to confirm the user and workspace, and the credits endpoint to check balance without consuming credits.
Rate limits are per workspace (HTTP 429 with Retry-After).

blockers.problem: Keys are tied to a user
blockers.fix: If that user leaves, the key may break. Use a service account.

blockers.problem: Tables API is Enterprise only and read-only
blockers.fix: Plan for it or use routines.
Budget and use the credit-balance endpoint.

automation.agentCan: Install the Clay CLI or plugin, write the API client and webhook verifier, create routines, and run test calls.
automation.humanMust: Own the Clay workspace and plan, create or approve the API key, and negotiate Enterprise if Tables are needed.

uncertain: Who can create keys (roles), whether inbound webhooks into tables exist and their plan limits (not covered in the pages read), numeric rate limits, and any OAuth plans.
The Public API docs appear new; older Clay guidance may differ.
